_comment: Parsing rules for bank notifications. Data, not code: every bank formats
differently, formats change without notice, and this app's audience uses
institutions no developer will ever hold an account with.
Each rule is a package matcher plus one regular expression with named
groups. The group names ARE the field mapping: amount, currency, balance
and merchant are read out of the match by name.
Patterns are matched case-insensitively against title and body joined by
a newline, with dotAll on. Anchor loosely: banks reword their prose more
often than they change its shape.
Every amount ends with lookaheads forbidding a further digit and a further
decimal group. Without both, a greedy match turns 45.5001 into 45.500, or
backtracks to 45 - a silently truncated figure, the worst thing it can do.
A rule with no `direction` infers it from debitKeywords/creditKeywords.
If both or neither appear the message is treated as ambiguous and
dropped, because guessing which way money moved is a coin flip.
`packages: []` matches any app. Use it only with a pattern specific
enough to stand on its own.

rules._comment: The shape most English-language bank alerts share: a verb, an amount with its currency, and often a resulting balance.
Alerts that lead with the amount: 'JOD 45.500 has been debited from...'.
Arabic alerts. Amounts arrive in Western or Arabic-Indic digits; Money.parse accepts both.

Symbols only, for the currencies where a symbol is unambiguous. The dollar sign is deliberately absent: it could be USD, CAD, AUD or a dozen more, and guessing is unacceptable in an app whose premise is knowing which currency you hold.
